questions.q: In 'The Wolf and the Shepherd', what happened when the Shepherd left his flock in the Wolf's care?
choices: Many Sheep were killed and carried off
The Wolf kept every Sheep safe
The Sheep ran away to the hills
questions.evidence: saw how many of the flock had been killed and carried off

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Wolf and the Shepherd'?
choices: Once a wolf, always a wolf
Wolves can learn to be good
questions.evidence: Once a wolf, always a wolf.

questions.q: In 'The Peacock and the Crane', how did the Crane answer the Peacock's bragging?
choices: He flew up toward the sun and said 'Follow me if you can'
He showed his own colorful tail
He pecked at the Peacock's feathers
questions.evidence: The Crane spread his broad wings and flew up toward the sun.

questions.q: In 'The Farmer and the Cranes', why did the Cranes stop being afraid of the Farmer at first?
choices: He swung his sling with no stones, so none of them got hurt
questions.evidence: they soon began to see that none of them ever got hurt

questions.q: In 'The Farmer and the Cranes', what finally made the Cranes stay away for good?
choices: The Farmer loaded his sling with stones
questions.evidence: he loaded his sling with stones and killed several of the Cranes

questions.q: In 'The Farmer and His Sons', what was the 'treasure' the sons really found?
choices: A big crop from all their hard digging
questions.evidence: the treasure their father had told them about was the wealth of a bountiful crop

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Farmer and His Sons'?
choices: Hard work is itself a treasure
Gold is hidden on every farm

questions.q: In 'The Two Pots', what happened to the Earthen Pot?
choices: It cracked and broke into a thousand pieces
It stayed safe by the fire
The Brass Pot carried it home
It grew stronger on the trip
questions.evidence: at the next jolt he flew into a thousand pieces

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Two Pots'?
